title: Docsmith SDK Playbook Scraps
content:
Quick scratchpad for SDK/tut fixes, sample app ideas, and things to carry between standups. Rough — mostly for my own memory.

Context: running through the Node + Python quickstarts; noticed a couple of places where the examples diverge from the runtime behaviour (streaming vs non-streaming, token param names). Goal: produce a small playbook that devs can copy into a repo, and a trimmed tutorial for hosted API + Dedicated notes.

Top-level TODOs (high priority):
- [ ] Finish compact Node sample that shows streaming + function-calling fallback (DOCS-4123) — target: EOD Fri
- [ ] Add a short note on batching behavior for embeddings vs text-generation (placement: "Optimize" doc section)
- [ ] Fix mismatched param names in python/quickstart.md (maxTokens -> max_tokens) — file is out of sync with SDK v0.12.
- [ ] Create a micro-sample repo: "rw-inference-playground/simple-chat" with both hosted + private config examples and a docker-compose for local testing.

Observations / bugs found while testing (raw):
- Streaming example in node-quickstart shows `res.on('data', ...)` but our SDK returns an AsyncIterable instead. Need to either update sample or add a wrapper snippet.
- Python snippet uses `client.generate(model='gpt-xyz', prompt=...)` but the current client API is `client.text.generate` after 0.12 split. Small but confusing for newcomers.
- Embedding doc claims 768-dim models under "small" category; backend catalog labels them as 1024. Where did this divergence happen? Possibly model catalog update in late Feb.

Small code notes to include in samples: (feel free to copy/paste)

Node streaming wrapper (PLACEHOLDER, needs testing):

const streamToConsole = async (iterable) => {
  for await (const chunk of iterable) {
    process.stdout.write(chunk.text || chunk);
  }
};

// usage
const resp = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood/gpt-fast', input: 'hi' });
await streamToConsole(resp);

(Need to confirm `resp` shape — is it an async generator of tokens or events?)

Python quick pitfall snippet:

# old
resp = client.generate(model='gpt-xyz', prompt='hello')

# new
resp = client.text.generate(model='gpt-xyz', prompt='hello')

Add a short note about "model variant fallback" — how Hosted routes can fallback to a cheaper quantized variant when capacity is constrained. This is a product behaviour that the sample app should optionally demonstrate via config flags: `preferred_variants: ['fast', 'quantized']`.

UX copy / doc gaps to address:
- Quickstart landing page should call out expected SDK minor version (e.g., "tested on rw-sdk 0.12.x"). Add a banner/alert box on top of the page.
- Provide an example that shows `timeoutMs` and `maxLatencyMs` tradeoffs for Dedicated customers. Short table: expected QPS vs recommended batch sizes. (I can draft numbers after SRE sync)
- Missing example: "embedding search + caching" — show a tiny 3-file example: ingest -> local LRU cache -> query. Make this a separate micro-tutorial.

Ideas for sample app (MVP):
- repo: rw-inference-playground/simple-chat
- components:
  - server/ : express + rw-sdk node sample with streaming + fallback
  - worker/ : python ingestion pipeline for embeddings, uses Redis for cache
  - infra/ : docker-compose to stand up redis + mock private deployment env (env var toggles to show private vs hosted)
  - README: clear steps for "run local in hosted mode" vs "run local in private mode"

Notes on docs process / checklist for each fix:
- Reproduce locally and add a small automated smoke test where feasible (jest for node samples, pytest for python).
- Create a small linked PR with changes and a single-sentence description for the release notes.
- Tag "devx-review" in the PR and add to the weekly docs triage board (DOCS-BOARD).

Open questions to resolve with Kai:
- Do we want to standardize on `text.generate` vs `generate` across SDKs, or keep language idioms? My vote: explicit namespaces (text, chat, embeddings) reduce accidental breakage in multi-function clients.
- How much of the sample repo should be copyable into customer sandboxes? (I think keep it minimal — no secrets, but show env var placeholders for KMS/HSM).

Meeting notes (from quick sync 2026-03-12):
- Kai: prefers sample app with CLI-first UX so it's easy to demo in 10m.
- Noah: wants a separate tutorial for "migrating from older SDKs" to reduce support noise. Good candidate for a short blog-style doc.
- Action: I will sketch the CLI UX tomorrow and wireframe README commands.

Micro timeline (my plan):
- Thu 3/12: finish Node streaming wrapper + confirm shape of async iterable (manual run).
- Fri 3/13: PR for python quickstart param fixes + tests.
- Mon 3/16: scaffold simple-chat repo, add README + demo script.
- Tue 3/17: pair with Kai for CLI polish, and open 'docs' PR with quickstart banner.

Misc scratch thoughts (copy out later):
- Consider adding a tiny Explore page in docs that surfaces "latest tested SDK version" per language, auto-generated from CI.
- Add a note in Dedicated docs about "burst capacity" vs "reserved" — sample config snippet.

Links I should annotate in PRs:
- ticket: DOCS-4123 (Node streaming samples)
- ticket: DOCS-4182 (Python API rename)
- GH PR template: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-docs/.github/pull_request_template.md

---
End of scratch — move actionable items to proper tickets after finish runs.

If you read this and want to grab anything: pls DM me (elena) or create a PR against `rw-inference-playground/simple-chat` and tag me.
